topics.name: Moles and Molar Mass

topics.name: Periodic Trends

topics.name: Valence Electrons and Ionic Compounds
topics.description: Use valence electrons and periodic position to predict ion charges, reactivity, and ionic formulas.

topics.name: Types of Chemical Bonds

topics.name: Structure of Ionic Solids
topics.description: Represent the arrangement of cations and anions in an ionic solid.

topics.name: Structure of Metals and Alloys
topics.description: Represent metallic bonding, delocalized electrons, and substitutional or interstitial alloys.

topics.name: Lewis Diagrams

topics.name: Resonance and Formal Charge
topics.description: Use resonance and formal charge to compare Lewis structures or explain equivalent bonds.

topics.name: VSEPR and Hybridization
topics.description: Use electron domains to infer geometry, angles, polarity, hybridization, or sigma/pi bonding.

topics.name: Intermolecular and Interparticle Forces
topics.description: Explain intermolecular attraction, boiling points, vapor pressure, or related properties from molecular interactions.

topics.name: Properties of Solids

topics.name: Solids, Liquids, and Gases

topics.description: Use particle motion and speed distributions to explain gas properties or temperature effects.

topics.name: Solutions and Mixtures

topics.name: Stoichiometry
topics.description: Use reaction coefficients to calculate reactant/product quantities, limiting reagents, or yield.

topics.name: Introduction to Titration
topics.description: Use titration equivalence and reaction stoichiometry to determine amounts or concentration.

topics.name: Types of Chemical Reactions
topics.description: Identify precipitation, acid-base, or redox reactions and oxidation-state changes.

topics.name: Introduction to Acid-Base Reactions
topics.description: Identify proton donors/acceptors and conjugate acid-base pairs.

topics.name: Reaction Rates

topics.name: Concentration Changes Over Time
topics.description: Use time-dependent concentration plots, integrated laws, or chemical half-lives.

topics.name: Elementary Reactions
topics.description: Derive the rate law of a single elementary step from its molecularity.

topics.name: Collision Model

topics.name: Reaction Energy Profile
topics.description: Interpret activation energy and overall energy change on a single-step reaction profile.

topics.name: Introduction to Reaction Mechanisms
topics.description: Identify intermediates, catalysts, and net reactions in a multistep mechanism.

topics.name: Reaction Mechanism and Rate Law
topics.description: Derive or test rate laws for mechanisms with the first step rate-limiting.

topics.name: Pre-Equilibrium Approximation

topics.name: Multistep Reaction Energy Profile
topics.description: Interpret intermediates and activation barriers on multistep reaction profiles.

topics.name: Catalysis
topics.description: Explain how catalysts provide a different mechanism and alter reaction rates.

topics.name: Endothermic and Exothermic Processes
topics.description: Infer endothermic/exothermic behavior and energy direction from observations.

topics.name: Energy Diagrams
topics.description: Represent relative reactant/product energies for physical or chemical processes.

topics.name: Heat Transfer and Thermal Equilibrium
topics.description: Explain heat transfer through collisions until thermal equilibrium is reached.

topics.name: Heat Capacity and Calorimetry
topics.description: Calculate heating/cooling energy from heat capacity, mass, and temperature change; analyze calorimetry.

topics.name: Energy of Phase Changes
topics.description: Calculate phase-transition energy using amount and fusion/vaporization enthalpy; interpret heating curves.

topics.description: Relate reaction heat to molar reaction enthalpy and reacting amount.

topics.name: Bond Enthalpies
topics.description: Calculate reaction enthalpy using energies of bonds broken and formed.

topics.name: Enthalpy of Formation
topics.description: Calculate reaction enthalpy using standard formation enthalpies.

topics.name: Hess’s Law
topics.description: Combine or reverse reaction steps and add their enthalpy changes using Hess's law.

topics.name: Introduction to Equilibrium
topics.description: Describe dynamic equilibrium and connect reversibility to observations.

topics.name: Direction of Reversible Reactions
topics.description: Predict net reaction direction from forward and reverse rates.

topics.name: Reaction Quotient and Equilibrium Constant

topics.name: Calculating the Equilibrium Constant
topics.description: Calculate equilibrium constants from measured equilibrium concentrations or pressures.

topics.name: Magnitude of the Equilibrium Constant

topics.name: Properties of the Equilibrium Constant
topics.description: Transform K when reversing, scaling, or adding chemical equations.

topics.name: Calculating Equilibrium Concentrations
topics.description: Calculate equilibrium concentrations or pressures from initial conditions and K.

topics.name: Representations of Equilibrium
topics.description: Interpret or construct particulate representations of equilibrium composition.

topics.name: Introduction to Le Châtelier’s Principle
topics.description: Predict equilibrium shifts due to concentration, temperature, or volume changes.

topics.name: Reaction Quotient and Le Châtelier’s Principle

topics.name: Introduction to Solubility Equilibria
topics.description: Relate molar solubility and Ksp; analyze precipitation using ionic concentration products.

topics.name: Common-Ion Effect
topics.description: Explain or calculate how a common ion changes salt solubility.

topics.name: Introduction to Acids and Bases
topics.description: Relate water autoionization, Kw, pH, pOH, and neutral conditions.

topics.name: pH and pOH of Strong Acids and Bases
topics.description: Calculate pH or pOH for strong-acid or strong-base solutions.

topics.name: Weak Acid and Base Equilibria
topics.description: Use Ka or Kb to find weak-acid/base equilibrium composition, pH, or percent ionization.

topics.name: Acid-Base Reactions and Buffers
topics.description: Determine major species and concentrations after mixing strong/weak acids and bases, including buffer formation.

topics.name: Acid-Base Titrations
topics.description: Interpret acid-base titration curves, equivalence points, half-equivalence, indicators, and species present.

topics.name: Molecular Structure of Acids and Bases
topics.description: Explain acid/base strength using molecular structure, bonds, polarity, or resonance.

topics.name: pH and pKa
topics.description: Use pH relative to pKa to identify the predominant protonation state.

topics.name: Properties of Buffers
topics.description: Explain how a conjugate acid-base pair resists pH change through reactions with added acid/base.

topics.name: Henderson-Hasselbalch Equation
topics.description: Determine buffer pH from pKa and conjugate-pair concentrations.

topics.name: Buffer Capacity
topics.description: Compare buffer capacities using amounts and ratios of acid/base components.

topics.name: pH and Solubility

topics.name: Introduction to Entropy
topics.description: Predict entropy trends or signs of entropy changes from particle dispersal.

topics.name: Absolute Entropy and Entropy Change
topics.description: Calculate reaction entropy using standard molar entropies.

topics.name: Gibbs Free Energy and Thermodynamic Favorability
topics.description: Use Gibbs free energy, enthalpy, entropy, and temperature to determine thermodynamic favorability.

topics.name: Thermodynamic and Kinetic Control
topics.description: Distinguish thermodynamic favorability from the kinetic rate of a process.

topics.name: Free Energy and Equilibrium

topics.name: Free Energy of Dissolution

topics.name: Coupled Reactions

topics.name: Galvanic (Voltaic) and Electrolytic Cells
topics.description: Analyze electrochemical cell components, half-cell reactions, electron/ion flow, and operation.

topics.name: Cell Potential and Free Energy
topics.description: Relate standard cell potential, Gibbs free energy, and electrochemical favorability.

topics.name: Cell Potential Under Nonstandard Conditions
topics.description: Explain qualitative concentration and nonstandard-condition effects on cell potential.

topics.name: Electrolysis and Faraday’s Law
